meta.title: Scarlet Thread: sources and bibliography
notes: works lists every work the site cites, with full publication details. group puts it under a heading on the Sources page. short is the name used in a Sources line.

nodes, edges, links, paths, and timeline say which work is cited where. A key under edges is the two stop ids joined by >, earlier stop first, as in the graph file. A key under links is the id in cross-links.json. A key under timeline is the id in timeline.json.
Each citation has work (an id from works), at (the section, chapter, or verse commented on), and says (one plain sentence on what the work is cited for).
The Westminster sections a stop quotes under Go deepest come from confessions.json and are added to its Sources by the app. Do not repeat them here.
scripture adds Scripture references to a stop's Sources line beyond the ones already in the graph and deeper files.

Never invent a citation. Cite a work only for what it says, and only as closely as it has been checked: the author, the title, and the chapter or the verse commented on. Give a page number only when it has been confirmed from the book itself. If a claim has no checked source, soften the claim or list it as source needed. Do not guess.
Never use an en dash or an em dash. Write ranges with the word to.

intro: Every stop, line, and date on this site rests on something you can check. Scripture comes first. Where the site explains a passage, gives a date, or states a doctrine, it names the work it leans on.

The Westminster Confession and Catechisms are cited by chapter and section, or by question number. Commentaries are cited by the verse they comment on. Other books are cited by chapter. A page number is given only where it was checked in the book itself, so most entries have none.
A work is cited only for what it says. Where faithful Reformed teachers differ, as on the thousand years of Revelation 20, a work is listed for each view and the site does not take a side.
Open any stop and look for Sources. Each name there is a link back to this page.

jesus.says: Our mediator was called Christ because he was anointed with the Holy Spirit to be prophet, priest, and king.

Calvin's chapter on how the Old Testament and the New agree.

On Genesis 3:15 as the opening promise of redemption.

Young reads the verse as a direct prophecy of the virgin birth of Christ.

magi.says: Calvin calls the Magi the firstfruits of the Gentiles.

The sum of the first four commandments is to love the Lord our God with all our heart, soul, strength, and mind.

dt_prophet.says: Calvin takes a prophet to stand for the whole line of prophets God would send, and says it is not to be limited to Christ alone.

How Christ carries out the office of a prophet.

dt_hanged.says: Calvin says Christ hung on the cross and so came under that curse, not for his own sake, but so that our curse was laid on him.

dt_song.says: God is most just, and also most loving, gracious, merciful, and long-suffering.

nt_greatest.says: The sum of the ten commandments is to love the Lord our God with all our heart, soul, strength, and mind, and our neighbor as ourselves.

is_call.says: Calvin says John tells us the Lord whom Isaiah saw was Christ (John 12:41). He adds that the vision should not be limited to the person of the Son.
God, as a righteous judge, blinds and hardens wicked people for their former sins.

is_immanuel.says: Christ was conceived by the power of the Holy Spirit in the womb of the virgin Mary.
The only redeemer of God's elect is the Lord Jesus Christ, who, being the eternal Son of God, became man.
Calvin says the prophet spoke of Christ. He knows the view that a child of that time is meant and does not accept it.
Young reads the verse as a direct prophecy of the virgin birth of Christ.

Christ was anointed with the Holy Spirit above measure.

Dates Sennacherib's campaign against Judah to 701 BC.

is_comfort.says: Justification is an act of God's free grace, in which he pardons all our sins.

is_servant_chosen.says: Calvin says the prophet here turns to speak of Christ.

is_cyrus.says: God upholds, directs, and governs all creatures, actions, and things, from the greatest to the least.
God ordains whatever comes to pass, yet the liberty of second causes is not taken away.
God's works of providence are his preserving and governing all his creatures and all their actions.
The Babylonian record of the fall of Babylon to Cyrus in 539 BC.
Cyrus's own account of taking Babylon and sending captive peoples home.
Argues that Isaiah the son of Amoz wrote the whole book.
Treats the whole book as the work of Isaiah.

Under the New Testament, grace and salvation are held out to all nations.

is_servant_suffering.says: Calvin says that by his death our sins have been expiated and salvation obtained for us.
The Lord Jesus, by his perfect obedience and the sacrifice of himself, has fully satisfied the justice of his Father.
Christ made a proper, real, and full satisfaction to his Father's justice for all who are justified.
Christ laid down his life an offering for sin.

is_invitation.says: God freely offers sinners life and salvation by Jesus Christ.
In effectual calling God's Spirit persuades and enables us to embrace Jesus Christ, freely offered to us in the gospel.
Effectual calling is the work of God's almighty power and grace.

is_anointed.says: Calvin says Christ rightly applies this prophecy to himself, and that it also fits the other prophets God anointed.
The Lord Jesus was anointed with the Holy Spirit above measure.

is_new_creation.says: Calvin reads the promise of the restoring of the church, begun after Babylon and carried through the whole reign of Christ to his last coming. He says the kingdom of Christ is here described under figures.
At the last day there will be a general resurrection of the dead, both of the just and the unjust.
God has appointed a day in which he will judge the world in righteousness by Jesus Christ.
The new earth is this creation renewed, not a different one put in its place.
The world to come is this creation renewed.

isn_mt1.says: Christ was conceived by the power of the Holy Spirit in the womb of the virgin Mary.
Calvin says the prophet spoke of Christ.

isn_mt4.says: Calvin says Matthew applied this passage to Christ correctly, and in its true meaning.

isn_lk4.says: How Christ carries out the office of a prophet.
The Lord Jesus was anointed with the Holy Spirit above measure.
Calvin says Christ rightly applies this prophecy to himself.

isn_jn12.says: Calvin says John tells us the Lord whom Isaiah saw was Christ.
God, as a righteous judge, blinds and hardens wicked people for their former sins.
God ordains whatever comes to pass, yet he is not the author of sin, and the will of his creatures is not forced.

isn_acts8.says: The Spirit of God makes the reading, and especially the preaching, of the word a means of drawing sinners to Christ.
The sure rule for interpreting Scripture is Scripture itself.

isn_1pet2.says: The Lord Jesus, by the sacrifice of himself, has fully satisfied the justice of his Father.
Christ carries out the office of a priest by once offering himself a sacrifice for the sins of his people.

isn_rev21.says: At the day of judgment the righteous will be received into heaven and made perfectly holy and happy in body and soul.
At the last day all the dead will be raised with the selfsame bodies.
The new earth is this creation renewed, not a different one put in its place.
The world to come is this creation renewed.

rv_christ.says: Christ's exaltation is his rising from the dead, going up into heaven, sitting at the right hand of God the Father, and coming to judge the world at the last day.
Seated at God's right hand, Christ gathers and defends his church.
The vision was seen almost in our own day, toward the end of Domitian's reign.
John was sent to Patmos under Domitian. Eusebius quotes Irenaeus for it.
Beale judges a date under Domitian more probable, and a date under Nero possible.
Most scholars date the book to the mid 90s. Some argue for a date under Nero, before AD 70.

rv_churches.says: There is no other head of the church but the Lord Jesus Christ.
The purest churches under heaven are subject both to mixture and error.
Christ as king gives his people officers, laws, and censures, and corrects them for their sins.

rv_throne.says: God's works of providence are his most holy, wise, and powerful preserving and governing all his creatures and all their actions.
God upholds, directs, and governs all creatures, actions, and things.

rv_lamb.says: Christ's humiliation, down to the cursed death of the cross.
Christ bought reconciliation and an everlasting inheritance for all those whom the Father has given to him.
To all for whom Christ bought redemption he certainly applies it.

rv_seals.says: Christ as king restrains and overcomes all the enemies of his people and orders all things for his glory and their good.
Hendriksen takes the rider on the white horse as Christ.
Beale takes the first rider as a satanic force that oppresses believers.

rv_multitude.says: Those whom God has accepted, called, and sanctified can neither totally nor finally fall away from the state of grace.
Their perseverance rests on God's unchanging love and decree, on Christ's merit and intercession, and on the Spirit who abides in them. It does not rest on their own free will.
Hendriksen takes the sealed as the whole church on earth, and the great multitude as the church in heaven.
Beale takes the 144,000 and the great multitude as the same group, the whole people of God.
Johnson notes that John hears the 144,000 and sees the countless host, two pictures of one people.

rv_trumpets.says: Hendriksen says the book has seven sections that run side by side, each spanning the time from Christ's first coming to his second. He calls this progressive parallelism.

rv_dragon.says: Calvin takes the offspring first as the woman's descendants as a whole. He then says the victory belongs to one head, Christ, and to his people in him.

An example of the Roman Catholic reading that the woman is Mary.

rv_beasts.says: The notes apply the beasts to the Roman empire and then to the popes of Rome.

God has appointed a day in which he will judge the world in righteousness by Jesus Christ.
